subject: MSA: alignment on notice windows & termination-for-convenience options
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acmeinc.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeinc.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA: notice windows & termination-for-convenience proposals

Team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Acme legal and procurement sketched out a few items we want to make sure are captured in the MSA/order form before we proceed to execution. Quick summary (attached is the schedule with our preferred timing):

- Auto-renew: Acme prefers opt-out at 60 days before term end rather than 30. We want a longer notice window to coordinate budgeting.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): we are proposing a 90-day notice to avoid disruption, but with a reduced transition credit if Redwood can provide a 30-day transition plan instead.
- Early-exit fee: if either party terminates for convenience mid-commitment, Acme would like a pro-rated credit (no flat fee) tied to remaining committed spend.
- Alignment: we need a single point of contact on Redwood side for procurement and legal redlines.

Attached: acme_notice_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet with preferred dates).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept 60-day opt-out and the TFC compromise (90-day with optional 30-day transition for reduced credit)? If not, what are your alternatives?

Jordan
Procurement Manager 
Acme, Inc.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA: notice windows & termination-for-convenience proposals

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary and the schedule. High level: we can get close, but need to align on a couple of points with legal and finance. Quick answers:

- Auto-renew/opt-out: 60 days is reasonable for larger enterprise deals. We typically standardize on 30 days for self-serve/customers, but for an ACV of this size we can make 60 days work if the order form flags the clause.
- TFC: we prefer a 60-day TFC to preserve service continuity and to avoid long tail capacity planning. That said, a 90-day TFC with an option for a 30-day transition plan in exchange for a specific credit carve-out is something we can discuss. We need to quantify the credit mechanics.
- Early-exit fee: we prefer a pro-rated remaining-committed-credit approach rather than a flat fee. The exact proration formula will need finance signoff.

I'll loop in legal to produce a redline for you to review. Karthik/Olga — can you take point on a draft redline that captures a 60-day opt-out, and two TFC paths (default 60-day; alternate 90-day w/ 30-day transition => X% credit)?

Sofia
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA: notice windows & termination-for-convenience proposals

Forwarding Acme's note — please see their schedule attached. Laura / Legal: we need a proposed redline for the MSA/order form. Key constraints from commercial: 60-day opt-out acceptable, prefer 60-day TFC; Acme may insist on a 90-day option with a reduced credit. Finance prefers a proration that equals remaining unused committed spend net of actual costs (we can model a 6-month smoothing).

Request from legal:
- Draft two TFC variants in the MSA (a) standard 60-day mutual termination for convenience; (b) customer-elected 90-day TFC with a defined transition credit if Redwood provides a 30-day expedited handoff.
- Define the proration formula and whether credits are issued as invoice credits or cash refunds.
- Confirm how the auto-renew notice will be implemented in the order form language (explicit 60-day opt-out if flagged).

Attachments: acme_notice_schedule.xlsx

Karthik
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acmeinc.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeinc.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA: notice windows & termination-for-convenience proposals

Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for laying this out. Attached is a redline (redlined_MSA_v3.docx) that implements the commercial direction with two TFC paths and the 60-day opt-out called out on the order form. High-level approach:

1) Auto-renew / Notice window
- Section 2.1 (Term and Renewal) now reads: "Unless Customer provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term, the Term shall automatically renew for successive renewal periods as set forth in the Order Form."
- Order Form will include a checkbox for enterprise customers to select the 60-day opt-out window.

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC) — two options
- Option A (Default): Mutual TFC with sixty (60) days' prior written notice. No early-exit credit other than standard invoicing/proration for usage-based charges.
- Option B (Customer-elected): Ninety (90) days' notice; Customer may elect an expedited 30-day transition plan delivered by Redwood in exchange for a transition credit equal to the pro-rated remainder of prepaid committed fees multiplied by 0.5 (50% of remaining committed fees).

3) Proration mechanics / credits
- Credits will be issued as invoice credits applied to future invoices within the next two billing cycles. Cash refunds only in exceptional cases and require Finance sign-off.
- The attached redline includes the proration formula and a worked example for a $600k annual commitment terminating after 7 months.

4) Implementation notes
- We'll flag the Order Form to show the selected TFC option and notice window.
- Legal requests Acme's confirmation of whether the transition credit percentage (50%) is acceptable or if you prefer a different split. If Acme wants the credit as a cash refund, note that we will need a Finance escalation and possibly an amendment to payment terms.

Next steps: if Jordan/Priya accept the credit mechanics, we'll finalize the redline and circulate for signature. If you'd like a different transition-credit % or a different proration period (e.g., 75% for 30-day expedited), propose it and we'll run it by Finance.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redlined_MSA_v3.docx (docx), acme_notice_schedule.xlsx (xlsx)
